title: Inmarsat Aero: P channel 10.5 kbit/s (A-QPSK) from the satellite
description: A synthetic GES's P channel at 10 500 bit/s, carrier +400 Hz off the VFO centre, arriving from 75 deg (the satellite: one transmitter, no talker). System table broadcasts, then a log-on confirm for AES 4CA2B1, an ACARS uplink to EI-ABC (label H1, 'METAR UPDATE FOLLOWS') and a C channel assignment, repeated. Expect the Channel fact 'P channel 10500 bit/s A-QPSK', every signal unit passing its CRC, those events, and the VFO's DoA (Digital squelch) at 75 deg. Measured through kraken_doa (2.5 loops): 26 signal units of 2444 lost per loop seam and in the first frame, the rest pass; DoA 75.0 deg steady; ~2 % of a core.

title: Inmarsat Aero: P channel 600 bit/s (A-BPSK) from the satellite
description: A synthetic GES's 600 bit/s P channel (frames of 2 s), carrier -1200 Hz off the VFO centre, from 220 deg. Acquisition takes a few seconds (the squared spectrum's lines at 600 Hz spacing), then system tables, a log-on confirm for AES C0FFEE and an ACARS uplink to C-GABC ('CLEARED AS FILED'). Expect 'P channel 600 bit/s A-BPSK', the events and the VFO's DoA at 220 deg. Measured through kraken_doa (2.2 loops): every signal unit after lock passes; DoA 220.0 deg steady; ~1 % of a core.

title: Inmarsat Aero: R / T bursts from four aircraft (1.2 and 0.6 kbit/s, 1.6 GHz)
description: Aircraft transmissions received directly (L-band uplink, 1645 MHz), the plugin in its 'R / T bursts' mode: AES 4CA2B1 (EI-ABC, 40 deg, carrier +300 Hz) sends an R channel log-on request and, in a T burst, an ADS-C report (flight EIN123) near the station; C0FFEE (C-GABC, 165 deg, -500 Hz) an ACARS downlink ('FUEL 0123') and a log-on request; A1B2C3 (VH-XYZ, 290 deg, +900 Hz) an ADS-C report (QFA001). 7C0123 (VH-OEJ, 330 deg, -1500 Hz) sends a long T burst at 600 bit/s (an ACARS downlink of 15 signal units, ~5 s). The bursts don't overlap. Each burst names its AES (24-bit ICAO address): expect talkers 4CA2B1, C0FFEE, A1B2C3, 7C0123 at those bearings and two aircraft on the map. Array radius 6 cm (0.39 wavelengths between neighbours at 1.6 GHz). Measured through kraken_doa (2.4 loops): every burst decoded, 14 of the 15 heard gave a bearing, bearings 40.0 / 165.0 / 290.0 / 330.0 deg; the VFO's own DoA follows whichever aircraft sent last, and 'Signal lost' comes between bursts.
steps: acars:7C0123:VH-OEJ:H1:4:LONG REPORT FOLLOWS - FUEL 0123 ALT FL350 SPEED M.82 WIND 270/45 TEMP M52 TURB NIL ICING NIL

title: Inmarsat Aero: C channel 8.4 kbit/s (voice) - framing and signalling
description: A synthetic to-aircraft C channel (8 400 bit/s A-QPSK, carrier -600 Hz) from 130 deg: unique words, the rate 2/3 code, 25 voice frames and three sub-band signal units per 500 ms frame, a call progress for AES 4CA2B1 every 2 s. The voice fields are random bits (no AMBE encoder is available to make speech): with the user's Aero AMBE library installed, Listen plays codec noise; without it the Voice codec fact says 'not installed' (or 'disabled'). Expect 'C channel 8400 bit/s', the call progress events and the VFO's DoA at 130 deg. Measured through kraken_doa (2.7 loops, Demod Digital, speaker on): with the codec, voice state 'voice - AES 4CA2B1' and ~90 % of the Opus packets carry sound (~3.7 % of a core); with KRAKEN_AERO_AMBE=none, the fact says 'disabled', the voice state 'AMBE codec not installed' and the audio stays silent. DoA 130.0 deg.

title: Inmarsat Aero: a 2.4 MHz band, every channel at once (All channels in the VFO)
description: A synthetic 2.4 MHz band around 1545.1 MHz (tools/aero_band.py, 12 s looped), the satellite at 120 deg: P channels at 600 (two, 5 kHz apart), 1200, 2400, 4800 and 10500 bit/s, an unmodulated carrier and a carrier of another system (a strong unmodulated part, 1200 Bd BPSK on it) between them, and a C channel at 1545.5 MHz that starts at 6.5 s after the 10500 bit/s channel assigned it (from 5 s). VFO 2.4 MHz, mode All channels in the VFO. Expect the channel list to show the six P channels and the C channel (opened by the assignment) and nothing at the two other carriers; events tagged with their channel: the log-on, the ACARS uplink to EI-ABC, the C channel assignment, the C channel call progress.
